title: Mathematical Operations and Symbols
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Mathematical Operations and Symbols. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

coverage: Meaning of arithmetic and comparison symbols

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Symbols and grouping

Parentheses, brackets and fraction bars group expressions. Exponentiation is evaluated before multiplication and addition; multiplication and division have equal precedence and are handled left to right, as are addition and subtraction. A fraction bar groups its entire numerator and denominator.

Absolute value and relations

Absolute value (|x|) is distance from zero, so it is nonnegative: (\(|x|=x\)) for (\(x \ge 0\)) and (\(|x|=-x\)) for (\(x<0\)). Symbols such as (\(<, \ge, \neq\)) compare values rather than perform arithmetic.

Defined operations

A question may define a new operation, for example (\(a star b=a^2+b\)). Use that definition exactly; it does not inherit familiar arithmetic properties unless they can be proved.

Worked example: With (\(a star b=2a-b\)), evaluate (\((3 star 1) star 2\)). First (\(3 star 1=5\)); then (\(5 star 2=8\)). The operation is not assumed associative.

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Rewrite complex expressions with explicit parentheses before calculating.
  • Use the defined-operation rule at every occurrence, including nested expressions.
  • Evaluate absolute value only after finding the sign of its contents.
  • Do not cancel terms across addition; cancellation applies to common factors.
  • Check whether a symbol is a relation, operation, unit or grouping mark.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Standard precedence: grouping, exponents/roots, multiplication/division left to right, addition/subtraction left to right.
  • (|a-b|) is the distance between numbers a and b on the number line.
  • (\(a^0=1\)) for (\(a \neq 0\)); zero to the zeroth power is not universally defined in elementary contexts.
  • For signed integers, subtraction is addition of the additive inverse.

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    If (\(a*b=a+b\)), what is (\(7*5\))?

    1. (\(2\))
    2. (\(12\))
    3. (\(35\))
    4. (\(75\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(12\))

    Replace the custom symbol using its definition: (\(7*5=7+5=12\)).

  2. Core:

    If (\(a\#b=a^2-b\)), find (\(5\#2\)).

    1. (\(13\))
    2. (\(21\))
    3. (\(23\))
    4. (\(27\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(23\))

    Substitute (\(a=5,b=2\)): (\(5^2-2=25-2=23\)).

  3. Foundation:

    Evaluate (\(18-6 \div 3 \times 2\)).

    1. (\(8\))
    2. (\(14\))
    3. (\(16\))
    4. (\(18\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(14\))

    Division and multiplication are evaluated left to right: (\(6 \div 3=2\)), then (\(2 \times 2=4\)); finally (\(18-4=14\)).

  4. Standard:

    If (\(a star b=a^2-b\)), find (\(3 star 4\)).

    1. (\(1\))
    2. (\(5\))
    3. (\(9\))
    4. (\(13\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(5\))

    Apply the definition: (\(3 star 4=3^2-4=9-4=5\)).

  5. Challenge:

    Solve (\(|x-4|=3\)).

    1. (\(x=1 only\))
    2. (\(x=7 only\))
    3. (\(x=1 or x=7\))
    4. (\(x=-1 or x=7\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(x=1 or x=7\))

    Absolute value 3 means (\(x-4=3\)) or (\(x-4=-3\)). Thus (\(x=7\)) or (\(x=1\)).
